section_1.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental difference between classical binary states (0 or 1) and quantum possibilities. Establish the hook: in the quantum world, things don't have to choose a side until we look at them.
section_1.example: A standard light switch is either 'ON' or 'OFF' (Classical). A quantum light switch is like a spinning coin on a table—while it's spinning, it is both Heads and Tails simultaneously.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Vector Map
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'State Space' using 2D geometry. Explain that a state can be represented as a vector (an arrow) on a graph where the X and Y axes represent the only two possible outcomes.
section_2.example: Draw a 2D coordinate system. Label the Y-axis as |Heads⟩ and the X-axis as |Tails⟩. A vector pointing straight up is 100% Heads.

section_3.title: Defining the Quantum State (|ψ⟩)
section_3.content: Introduce Dirac Notation (Bra-Ket). Define the quantum state |ψ⟩ (Psi) as a unit vector that can point anywhere between the axes. Explain that the 'length' of the vector must always be 1.
section_3.example: Show a character named 'Quarky the Cat'. Quarky's state is |ψ⟩. If the arrow is halfway between 'Awake' and 'Asleep', Quarky is in a linear combination of both.

section_4.title: The Math of Superposition
section_4.content: Present the superposition equation: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Use a graphical overlay to show that α (alpha) and β (beta) are the 'shadows' (projections) of the vector onto the axes. These are called probability amplitudes.
section_4.example: Visual: An arrow at a 45-degree angle. The projection on the X-axis is 0.707 (α) and on the Y-axis is 0.707 (β). Note that α² + β² = 1 (0.5 + 0.5 = 1).

section_5.title: The Collapse: The Act of Measuring
section_5.content: Explain that 'looking' at a quantum system forces it to choose a state. This is 'Wavefunction Collapse'. The probability of picking a state is the square of its amplitude (|α|² or |β|²).
section_5.example: Animation: A 'Measurement Camera' flashes at the diagonal vector. The vector instantly 'snaps' to either the vertical or horizontal axis. The diagonal state disappears, and we now have a definite classical result.

section_6.title: Application: Quantum Computing
section_6.content: Summarize why this matters. A classical bit (0 or 1) is a single path. A Qubit (superposition) represents multiple paths at once, allowing for massive parallel processing power.
section_6.example: A robot trying to find the exit of a maze. A classical robot tries one path at a time. A quantum robot in superposition acts like a gas, exploring every possible path simultaneously to find the exit instantly.

section_1.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental difference between classical binary states (0 or 1) and quantum possibilities. Establish the hook: in the quantum world, things don't have to choose a side until we look at them.
section_1.example: A standard light switch is either 'ON' or 'OFF' (Classical). A quantum light switch is like a spinning coin on a table—while it's spinning, it is both Heads and Tails simultaneously.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Vector Map
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'State Space' using 2D geometry. Explain that a state can be represented as a vector (an arrow) on a graph where the X and Y axes represent the only two possible outcomes.
section_2.example: Draw a 2D coordinate system. Label the Y-axis as |Heads⟩ and the X-axis as |Tails⟩. A vector pointing straight up is 100% Heads.

section_3.title: Defining the Quantum State (|ψ⟩)
section_3.content: Introduce Dirac Notation (Bra-Ket). Define the quantum state |ψ⟩ (Psi) as a unit vector that can point anywhere between the axes. Explain that the 'length' of the vector must always be 1.
section_3.example: Show a character named 'Quarky the Cat'. Quarky's state is |ψ⟩. If the arrow is halfway between 'Awake' and 'Asleep', Quarky is in a linear combination of both.

section_4.title: The Math of Superposition
section_4.content: Present the superposition equation: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Use a graphical overlay to show that α (alpha) and β (beta) are the 'shadows' (projections) of the vector onto the axes. These are called probability amplitudes.
section_4.example: Visual: An arrow at a 45-degree angle. The projection on the X-axis is 0.707 (α) and on the Y-axis is 0.707 (β). Note that α² + β² = 1 (0.5 + 0.5 = 1).

section_5.title: The Collapse: The Act of Measuring
section_5.content: Explain that 'looking' at a quantum system forces it to choose a state. This is 'Wavefunction Collapse'. The probability of picking a state is the square of its amplitude (|α|² or |β|²).
section_5.example: Animation: A 'Measurement Camera' flashes at the diagonal vector. The vector instantly 'snaps' to either the vertical or horizontal axis. The diagonal state disappears, and we now have a definite classical result.

section_6.title: Application: Quantum Computing
section_6.content: Summarize why this matters. A classical bit (0 or 1) is a single path. A Qubit (superposition) represents multiple paths at once, allowing for massive parallel processing power.
section_6.example: A robot trying to find the exit of a maze. A classical robot tries one path at a time. A quantum robot in superposition acts like a gas, exploring every possible path simultaneously to find the exit instantly.

- The camera flashes (brief white screen flash or bright circle).
- The vector snaps to the Y-axis |0⟩ (#FFFF00) instantly.
- Fade out the original diagonal vector and the α projection.

Lecture Lines:

2. Qubits explore every possible path simultaneously.
3. This allows computers to solve complex problems instantly.

Animations:
- Show a maze with one white dot moving through a path.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Quantum State (|ψ⟩)", [
            "We call this quantum state vector 'Ket Psi'.",
            "It can point anywhere between our two outcome axes.",
            "Crucially, the length of this arrow is always one."
        ])

        psi_color = "#FF69B4"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(psi_color)
        
        # Create a unit circle and axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE}
        )
        # We'll treat the area C2 to E5 as our canvas for the circle
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # The center of the axes is our origin
        origin = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        unit_circle = Arc(radius=axes.get_x_unit_size(), start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color=GRAY_A)
        unit_circle.move_to(origin, aligned_edge=DL)
        
        psi_label = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle", color=psi_color)
        self.place_at_grid(psi_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(unit_circle),
            Write(psi_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(psi_color)
        
        # Initial vector at 45 degrees
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(45 * DEGREES)

            "- Mathematical superposition combines these states using Greek letters.",
            "- Alpha and Beta represent the vector's horizontal and vertical shadows.",
            "- These 'amplitudes' define the probability of each outcome.",
            "- The squared sum of these shadows must equal one.",
            "- This ensures the total probability always remains one hundred percent."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the superposition equation: "|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩" (#FFFFFF).

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measuring a system forces it to pick one state.",
            "The vector instantly snaps to a single classical axis.",
            "This sudden change is known as 'Wavefunction Collapse'.",
            "Probability depends on the square of the state's amplitude.",
            "The mystery of 'both' vanishes upon our observation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Collapse: The Act of Measuring", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PSI = "#FF69B4"   # Pink from section 3
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for |0> (Y-axis)
        COLOR_ALPHA = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_BETA = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_CAMERA = "#CCCCCC" # Grey
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Coordinate system
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        label_0 = MathTex("|0\\rangle", color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(0.8)
        label_0.next_to(axes.c2p(0, 1), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        label_1 = MathTex("|1\\rangle", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        label_1.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Initial Vector |psi> at 45 degrees
        vec_end_init = axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5))
        vec_psi = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            end=vec_end_init,
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_PSI
        )
        label_psi = MathTex("|\\psi\\rangle", color=COLOR_PSI).scale(0.8)
        label_psi.next_to(vec_psi.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # Projections
        proj_alpha = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_ALPHA
        )
        proj_beta = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_BETA
        )
        
        label_alpha = MathTex("\\alpha", color=COLOR_ALPHA).scale(0.8)
        label_alpha.next_to(axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        label_beta = MathTex("\\beta", color=COLOR_BETA).scale(0.8)
        label_beta.next_to(axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Camera Icon
        camera_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.3, width=0.5, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=1)
        camera_lens = Circle(radius=0.08, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(camera_body.get_center())
        camera_top = Rectangle(height=0.08, width=0.12, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=1).next_to(camera_body, UP, buff=-0.05).shift(LEFT*0.1)
        camera = VGroup(camera_body, camera_lens, camera_top)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, 'A6', scale_factor=1.2)

        self.add(axes, label_0, label_1)
        self.play(Create(vec_psi), Write(label_psi))
        self.play(Create(proj_alpha), Create(proj_beta), Write(label_alpha), Write(label_beta))
        self.play(FadeIn(camera))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Preparation for snap: ghosts
        ghost_psi = vec_psi.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        ghost_proj_alpha = proj_alpha.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        ghost_label_alpha = label_alpha.copy().set_opacity(0.3)

        # Flash effect
        flash = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(camera.get_center())
        self.play(flash.animate.scale(50).set_opacity(0), run_time=0.4)
        self.remove(flash)
        
        # Add ghosts to scene
        self.add(ghost_psi, ghost_proj_alpha, ghost_label_alpha)

        # Vector snaps to Y-axis |0>
        target_end = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        self.play(
            vec_psi.animate.put_start_and_end_on(axes.c2p(0,0), target_end).set_color(COLOR_ZERO),
            label_psi.animate.next_to(target_end, UP, buff=0.1).set_color(COLOR_ZERO),
            proj_beta.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0),
            proj_alpha.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0),
            label_beta.animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO),
            run_time=0.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Emphasize collapse
        self.play(Indicate(vec_psi, color=COLOR_ZERO, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Show probability relationship
        prob_math = MathTex("P(|0\\rangle) = |\\beta|^2", color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_math, 'D6')
        
        self.play(Write(prob_math))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Fade out ghosts and extra indicators
        self.play(
            FadeOut(ghost_psi),
            FadeOut(ghost_proj_alpha),
            FadeOut(ghost_label_alpha),
            FadeOut(camera),
            FadeOut(label_alpha),
            FadeOut(label_beta),
            prob_math.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: Quantum Computing",
            [
                "Classical bits process one path at a time.",
                "Qubits explore every possible path simultaneously.",
                "This allows computers to solve complex problems instantly."
            ]
        )

        # Maze Setup in grid area B2 to E5
        tl = self.grid["B2"]
        br = self.grid["E5"]
        width = br[0] - tl[0]
        height = tl[1] - br[1] # height is negative magnitude
        
        def g(r, c):
            # Calculate node position within the B2-E5 area
            return tl + np.array([c * (width / 3), -r * (height / -3), 0])

        maze_walls = VGroup(
            Line(g(0,0), g(0,3)), # Top
            Line(g(3,0), g(3,3)), # Bottom
            Line(g(0,0), g(3,0)), # Left
            Line(g(0,3), g(3,3)), # Right
            # Internal Walls
            Line(g(1,0), g(1,2)),
            Line(g(2,1), g(2,3)),
            Line(g(0,1), g(2,1)),
            Line(g(1,2), g(3,2)),
        ).set_color(GRAY).set_stroke(width=4)

        start_label = Text("START", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(start_label, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        exit_label = Text("EXIT", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(exit_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.add(maze_walls, start_label, exit_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # White dot representing a classical bit
        white_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        white_dot.move_to(g(3,0))
        self.add(white_dot)
        
        # Sequential path: Start -> (3,1) -> (2,1) -> (1,1) -> (1,2) -> (0,2) -> (0,3)
        path = [g(3,1), g(2,1), g(1,1), g(1,2), g(0,2), g(0,3)]
        
        for pos in path:
            self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(pos), run_time=0.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset color and highlight second line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF") # Blue-Cyan color

        self.setup_layout("The Classical vs. Quantum Divide", lecture_lines)

        lever.shift(DOWN * 0.2)

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measuring a system forces it to pick one state.",
            "The vector instantly snaps to a single classical axis.",
            "This sudden change is known as 'Wavefunction Collapse'.",
            "Probability depends on the square of the state's amplitude.",
            "The mystery of 'both' vanishes upon our observation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Collapse: The Act of Measuring", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PSI = "#FF69B4"   # Pink from section 3
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for |0> (Y-axis)
        COLOR_ALPHA = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_BETA = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_CAMERA = "#CCCCCC" # Grey
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Coordinate system
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        label_0 = MathTex("|0\\rangle", color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(0.8)
        label_0.next_to(axes.c2p(0, 1), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        label_1 = MathTex("|1\\rangle", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        label_1.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Initial Vector |psi> at 45 degrees
        vec_end_init = axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5))
        vec_psi = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            end=vec_end_init,
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_PSI
        )
        label_psi = MathTex("|\\psi\\rangle", color=COLOR_PSI).scale(0.8)
        label_psi.next_to(vec_psi.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # Projections
        proj_alpha = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_ALPHA
        )
        proj_beta = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_BETA
        )
        
        label_alpha = MathTex("\\alpha", color=COLOR_ALPHA).scale(0.8)
        label_alpha.next_to(axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        label_beta = MathTex("\\beta", color=COLOR_BETA).scale(0.8)
        label_beta.next_to(axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Camera Icon
        camera_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.3, width=0.5, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=1)
        camera_lens = Circle(radius=0.08, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(camera_body.get_center())
        camera_top = Rectangle(height=0.08, width=0.12, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=1).next_to(camera_body, UP, buff=-0.05).shift(LEFT*0.1)
        camera = VGroup(camera_body, camera_lens, camera_top)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, 'A6', scale_factor=1.2)

        self.add(axes, label_0, label_1)
        self.play(Create(vec_psi), Write(label_psi))
        self.play(Create(proj_alpha), Create(proj_beta), Write(label_alpha), Write(label_beta))
        self.play(FadeIn(camera))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Preparation for snap: ghosts
        ghost_psi = vec_psi.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        ghost_proj_alpha = proj_alpha.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        ghost_label_alpha = label_alpha.copy().set_opacity(0.3)

        # Flash effect
        flash = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(camera.get_center())
        self.play(flash.animate.scale(50).set_opacity(0), run_time=0.4)
        self.remove(flash)
        
        # Add ghosts to scene
        self.add(ghost_psi, ghost_proj_alpha, ghost_label_alpha)

        # Vector snaps to Y-axis |0>
        target_end = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        self.play(
            vec_psi.animate.put_start_and_end_on(axes.c2p(0,0), target_end).set_color(COLOR_ZERO),

        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

section_1.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental difference between classical binary states (0 or 1) and quantum possibilities. Establish the hook: in the quantum world, things don't have to choose a side until we look at them.
section_1.example: A standard light switch is either 'ON' or 'OFF' (Classical). A quantum light switch is like a spinning coin on a table—while it's spinning, it is both Heads and Tails simultaneously.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Vector Map
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'State Space' using 2D geometry. Explain that a state can be represented as a vector (an arrow) on a graph where the X and Y axes represent the only two possible outcomes.
section_2.example: Draw a 2D coordinate system. Label the Y-axis as |Heads⟩ and the X-axis as |Tails⟩. A vector pointing straight up is 100% Heads.

section_3.title: Defining the Quantum State (|ψ⟩)
section_3.content: Introduce Dirac Notation (Bra-Ket). Define the quantum state |ψ⟩ (Psi) as a unit vector that can point anywhere between the axes. Explain that the 'length' of the vector must always be 1.
section_3.example: Show a character named 'Quarky the Cat'. Quarky's state is |ψ⟩. If the arrow is halfway between 'Awake' and 'Asleep', Quarky is in a linear combination of both.

section_4.title: The Math of Superposition
section_4.content: Present the superposition equation: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Use a graphical overlay to show that α (alpha) and β (beta) are the 'shadows' (projections) of the vector onto the axes. These are called probability amplitudes.
section_4.example: Visual: An arrow at a 45-degree angle. The projection on the X-axis is 0.707 (α) and on the Y-axis is 0.707 (β). Note that α² + β² = 1 (0.5 + 0.5 = 1).

section_5.title: The Collapse: The Act of Measuring
section_5.content: Explain that 'looking' at a quantum system forces it to choose a state. This is 'Wavefunction Collapse'. The probability of picking a state is the square of its amplitude (|α|² or |β|²).
section_5.example: Animation: A 'Measurement Camera' flashes at the diagonal vector. The vector instantly 'snaps' to either the vertical or horizontal axis. The diagonal state disappears, and we now have a definite classical result.

section_6.title: Application: Quantum Computing
section_6.content: Summarize why this matters. A classical bit (0 or 1) is a single path. A Qubit (superposition) represents multiple paths at once, allowing for massive parallel processing power.
section_6.example: A robot trying to find the exit of a maze. A classical robot tries one path at a time. A quantum robot in superposition acts like a gas, exploring every possible path simultaneously to find the exit instantly.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Classical systems exist in one definite state at once.",
            "A light switch is either strictly ON or OFF.",
            "Quantum systems are different; they don't choose sides yet.",
            "Imagine a spinning coin, being both heads and tails.",
            "This 'bothness' is the core of the quantum world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Classical vs. Quantum Divide", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        classical_text = Text("Classical: 0 or 1", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(classical_text, 'A1', 'A4')
        
        # Light switch base
        switch_base = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=1.0, color=GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(switch_base, 'B3')
        
        # Switch lever
        lever = Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.4, stroke_width=8, color=WHITE)
        # Move pivot (ORIGIN of the line) to center of base
        lever.move_to(switch_base.get_center() + UP * 0.2)
        lever_pivot = switch_base.get_center()
        lever.shift(DOWN * 0.2) 
        
        self.play(Write(classical_text), Create(switch_base), Create(lever))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Flip switch multiple times to show binary state
        self.play(lever.animate.rotate(PI/3, about_point=lever_pivot), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(lever.animate.rotate(-PI/3, about_point=lever_pivot), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(lever.animate.rotate(PI/3, about_point=lever_pivot), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        quantum_text = Text("Quantum: Both?", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(quantum_text, 'D1', 'D4')
        
        self.play(Write(quantum_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Coin setup
        coin = Circle(radius=0.7, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(coin, 'E3', 'F4')
        
        heads_label = Text("H", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        tails_label = Text("T", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        heads_label.move_to(coin.get_center())
        tails_label.move_to(coin.get_center())
        
        h_side_label = Text("Heads", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        t_side_label = Text("Tails", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(h_side_label, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(t_side_label, 'F5')

        # Tracker for rotation
        spin_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Group for the coin and its internal labels
        coin_group = VGroup(coin, heads_label, tails_label)
        
        # Updater for the spinning coin (visualizing superposition)
        def update_coin(m):
            val = spin_tracker.get_value()
            # Oscillation of width to simulate spin
            scale_x = np.cos(val * 2 * PI)
            m[0].stretch_to_fit_width(max(0.05, abs(scale_x) * 1.4))
            
            # Switch between showing H and T
            if scale_x > 0:
                m[1].set_opacity(1)
                m[2].set_opacity(0)
                m[1].stretch_to_fit_width(max(0.05, abs(scale_x) * 0.8))
            else:
                m[1].set_opacity(0)
                m[2].set_opacity(1)
                m[2].stretch_to_fit_width(max(0.05, abs(scale_x) * 0.8))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Quantum State (|ψ⟩)", [
            "We call this quantum state vector 'Ket Psi'.",
            "It can point anywhere between our two outcome axes.",
            "Crucially, the length of this arrow is always one."
        ])

        psi_color = "#FF69B4"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(psi_color)
        
        # Create a unit circle and axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE}
        )
        # We'll treat the area C2 to E5 as our canvas for the circle
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # The center of the axes is our origin
        origin = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        unit_circle = Arc(radius=axes.get_x_unit_size(), start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color=GRAY_A)
        unit_circle.move_to(origin, aligned_edge=DL)
        
        psi_label = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle", color=psi_color)
        self.place_at_grid(psi_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(unit_circle),
            Write(psi_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(psi_color)
        
        # Initial vector at 45 degrees
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(45 * DEGREES)
        
        def get_vector_end():
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            return axes.c2p(np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle))

        vector = always_redraw(lambda: Vector(
            get_vector_end() - origin, 
            color=psi_color
        ).shift(origin))
        
        # Note: per instruction 11, we shouldn't create new objects in always_redraw if expensive.
        # Vector is relatively cheap, but let's be careful. 
        # Actually, standard practice for simple geometric lines/vectors is okay, 
        # but the instructions say "Prefer persistent mobjects plus add_updater".
        
        # Revision using updater on a persistent Vector:
        vector_obj = Vector(axes.c2p(np.cos(45*DEGREES), np.sin(45*DEGREES)) - origin, color=psi_color).shift(origin)
        vector_obj.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            Vector(axes.c2p(np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())) - origin, color=psi_color).shift(origin)
        ))

        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_obj))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(psi_color)
        
        # Rotate smoothly
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(10 * DEGREES),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(80 * DEGREES),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(45 * DEGREES),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

            "- Mathematical superposition combines these states using Greek letters.",
            "- Alpha and Beta represent the vector's horizontal and vertical shadows.",
            "- These 'amplitudes' define the probability of each outcome.",
            "- The squared sum of these shadows must equal one.",
            "- This ensures the total probability always remains one hundred percent."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the superposition equation: "|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩" (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Vector at 45 degrees, length 1
        # sin(45) = cos(45) = 1/sqrt(2) approx 0.707

        vec_end = axes.c2p(val_0707, val_0707)
        vec_start = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        vector = Arrow(vec_start, vec_end, buff=0, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), GrowArrow(vector))
        self.wait(1)

        proj_y = DashedLine(vec_end, axes.c2p(0, val_0707), color=GRAY)

        label_beta = MathTex(r"\beta", color="#FF0000")

        label_beta.next_to(axes.c2p(0, val_0707/2), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(segment_x), Create(segment_y), Write(label_alpha), Write(label_beta))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Display and highlight "α² + β² = 1" (#FFFFFF) next to the vector.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        sum_eqn = MathTex(r"\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 1", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(sum_eqn, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(sum_eqn))
        self.play(Indicate(sum_eqn))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This ensures the total probability always remains one hundred percent.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        prob_text = Text("Total Probability = 100%", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        # Position slightly below the sum_eqn
        prob_text.move_to(sum_eqn.get_bottom() + DOWN * 0.4)
        
        self.play(Write(prob_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup or highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

            "This sudden change is known as 'Wavefunction Collapse'.",
            "Probability depends on the square of the state's amplitude.",
            "The mystery of 'both' vanishes upon our observation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Collapse: The Act of Measuring", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PSI = "#FF69B4"   # Pink from section 3
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for |0> (Y-axis)
        COLOR_ALPHA = "#00FF00" # Green

            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)),

        )

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: Quantum Computing",
            [
                "Classical bits process one path at a time.",
                "Qubits explore every possible path simultaneously.",
                "This allows computers to solve complex problems instantly."
            ]
        )

        # Maze Setup in grid area B2 to E5
        tl = self.grid["B2"]
        br = self.grid["E5"]
        width = br[0] - tl[0]
        height = tl[1] - br[1] # height is negative magnitude
        
        def g(r, c):
            # Calculate node position within the B2-E5 area
            return tl + np.array([c * (width / 3), -r * (height / -3), 0])

        maze_walls = VGroup(
            Line(g(0,0), g(0,3)), # Top
            Line(g(3,0), g(3,3)), # Bottom
            Line(g(0,0), g(3,0)), # Left
            Line(g(0,3), g(3,3)), # Right
            # Internal Walls
            Line(g(1,0), g(1,2)),
            Line(g(2,1), g(2,3)),
            Line(g(0,1), g(2,1)),
            Line(g(1,2), g(3,2)),
        ).set_color(GRAY).set_stroke(width=4)

        start_label = Text("START", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(start_label, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        exit_label = Text("EXIT", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(exit_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.add(maze_walls, start_label, exit_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # White dot representing a classical bit
        white_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        white_dot.move_to(g(3,0))
        self.add(white_dot)
        
        # Sequential path: Start -> (3,1) -> (2,1) -> (1,1) -> (1,2) -> (0,2) -> (0,3)
        path = [g(3,1), g(2,1), g(1,1), g(1,2), g(0,2), g(0,3)]
        
        for pos in path:
            self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(pos), run_time=0.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset color and highlight second line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF") # Blue-Cyan color
        
        # Move white dot back to start for comparison
        self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(g(3,0)), run_time=0.5)

        # Create many blue dots to represent a superposition "gas"
        blue_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) for _ in range(13)])
        for dot in blue_dots:
            dot.move_to(g(3,0))
        self.add(blue_dots)

        # Destinations for dots to simulate "filling" the maze
        destinations = [
            g(3,1), g(3,2), g(3,3),
            g(2,0), g(2,1), g(2,2),
            g(1,0), g(1,1), g(1,2),
            g(0,0), g(0,1), g(0,2), g(0,3)
        ]

        # Animate blue dots spreading simultaneously
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[dot.animate.move_to(dest) for dot, dest in zip(blue_dots, destinations)],
                lag_ratio=0.05
            ),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset color and highlight third line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # The dot at the exit pulses
        exit_qubit = blue_dots[-1] # The one that reached g(0,3)
        
        # While the exit is "found" by the qubit, the classical dot starts moving again
        self.play(
            Indicate(exit_qubit, color=GREEN, scale_factor=1.5),
            white_dot.animate.move_to(g(3,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Show classical dot still trying while quantum is done
        self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(g(2,1)), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measuring a system forces it to pick one state.",
            "The vector instantly snaps to a single classical axis.",
            "This sudden change is known as 'Wavefunction Collapse'.",
            "Probability depends on the square of the state's amplitude.",
            "The mystery of 'both' vanishes upon our observation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Collapse: The Act of Measuring", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PSI = "#FF69B4"   # Pink from section 3
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for |0> (Y-axis)
        COLOR_ALPHA = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_BETA = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_CAMERA = "#CCCCCC" # Grey
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Coordinate system
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        label_0 = MathTex("|0\\rangle", color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(0.8)
        label_0.next_to(axes.c2p(0, 1), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        label_1 = MathTex("|1\\rangle", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        label_1.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Initial Vector |psi> at 45 degrees
        vec_end_init = axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5))
        vec_psi = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            end=vec_end_init,
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_PSI
        )
        label_psi = MathTex("|\\psi\\rangle", color=COLOR_PSI).scale(0.8)
        label_psi.next_to(vec_psi.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # Projections
        proj_alpha = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_ALPHA
        )
        proj_beta = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_BETA
        )
        
        label_alpha = MathTex("\\alpha", color=COLOR_ALPHA).scale(0.8)
        label_alpha.next_to(axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        label_beta = MathTex("\\beta", color=COLOR_BETA).scale(0.8)
        label_beta.next_to(axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        camera_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.3, width=0.5, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=1)
        camera_lens = Circle(radius=0.08, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(camera_body.get_center())
        camera_top = Rectangle(height=0.08, width=0.12, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=1).next_to(camera_body, UP, buff=-0.05).shift(LEFT*0.1)
        camera = VGroup(camera_body, camera_lens, camera_top)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, 'A6', scale_factor=1.2)

        self.add(axes, label_0, label_1)
        self.play(Create(vec_psi), Write(label_psi))
        self.play(Create(proj_alpha), Create(proj_beta), Write(label_alpha), Write(label_beta))
        self.play(FadeIn(camera))
        self.wait(1)

        self.remove(flash)
        
        # Add ghosts to scene

        # Vector snaps to Y-axis |0>

        )
        self.play(

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: Quantum Computing",
            [
                "Classical bits process one path at a time.",
                "Qubits explore every possible path simultaneously.",
                "This allows computers to solve complex problems instantly."
            ]
        )

        # Maze Setup in grid area B2 to E5
        tl = self.grid["B2"]
        br = self.grid["E5"]
        width = br[0] - tl[0]
        height = tl[1] - br[1] # height is negative magnitude
        
        def g(r, c):
            # Calculate node position within the B2-E5 area
            return tl + np.array([c * (width / 3), -r * (height / -3), 0])

        maze_walls = VGroup(
            Line(g(0,0), g(0,3)), # Top
            Line(g(3,0), g(3,3)), # Bottom
            Line(g(0,0), g(3,0)), # Left
            Line(g(0,3), g(3,3)), # Right
            # Internal Walls
            Line(g(1,0), g(1,2)),
            Line(g(2,1), g(2,3)),
            Line(g(0,1), g(2,1)),
            Line(g(1,2), g(3,2)),
        ).set_color(GRAY).set_stroke(width=4)

        start_label = Text("START", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(start_label, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        exit_label = Text("EXIT", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(exit_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.add(maze_walls, start_label, exit_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # White dot representing a classical bit
        white_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        white_dot.move_to(g(3,0))
        self.add(white_dot)
        
        # Sequential path: Start -> (3,1) -> (2,1) -> (1,1) -> (1,2) -> (0,2) -> (0,3)
        path = [g(3,1), g(2,1), g(1,1), g(1,2), g(0,2), g(0,3)]
        
        for pos in path:
            self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(pos), run_time=0.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset color and highlight second line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF") # Blue-Cyan color
        
        # Move white dot back to start for comparison
        self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(g(3,0)), run_time=0.5)

        # Create many blue dots to represent a superposition "gas"
        blue_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) for _ in range(13)])
        for dot in blue_dots:
            dot.move_to(g(3,0))
        self.add(blue_dots)

        # Destinations for dots to simulate "filling" the maze
        destinations = [
            g(3,1), g(3,2), g(3,3),
            g(2,0), g(2,1), g(2,2),
            g(1,0), g(1,1), g(1,2),
            g(0,0), g(0,1), g(0,2), g(0,3)
        ]

        # Animate blue dots spreading simultaneously
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[dot.animate.move_to(dest) for dot, dest in zip(blue_dots, destinations)],
                lag_ratio=0.05
            ),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset color and highlight third line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # The dot at the exit pulses
        exit_qubit = blue_dots[-1] # The one that reached g(0,3)
        
        # While the exit is "found" by the qubit, the classical dot starts moving again
        self.play(
            Indicate(exit_qubit, color=GREEN, scale_factor=1.5),
            white_dot.animate.move_to(g(3,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Show classical dot still trying while quantum is done
        self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(g(2,1)), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

Alpha and Beta represent the vector's horizontal and vertical shadows.
These 'amplitudes' define the probability of each outcome.
The squared sum of these shadows must equal one.
This ensures the total probability always remains one hundred percent.

        self.setup_layout("The Math of Superposition", [

        vec_start = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        vector = Arrow(vec_start, vec_end, buff=0, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), GrowArrow(vector))
        self.wait(1)

        proj_y = DashedLine(vec_end, axes.c2p(0, val_0707), color=GRAY)

        label_beta = MathTex(r"\beta", color="#FF0000")

        label_alpha.next_to(axes.c2p(val_0707/2, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        sum_eqn = MathTex(r"\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 1", color=WHITE)

outline.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
outline.content: Introduce the fundamental difference between classical binary states (0 or 1) and quantum possibilities. Establish the hook: in the quantum world, things don't have to choose a side until we look at them.
outline.example: A standard light switch is either 'ON' or 'OFF' (Classical). A quantum light switch is like a spinning coin on a table—while it's spinning, it is both Heads and Tails simultaneously.

storyboard.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
lecture_lines: Classical systems exist in one definite state at once.
A light switch is either strictly ON or OFF.
Quantum systems are different; they don't choose sides yet.
Imagine a spinning coin, being both heads and tails.
This "bothness" is the core of the quantum world.
animations: Display text "Classical: 0 or 1" (#FFFFFF) and show a light switch [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/switch.svg] flipping.
Display text "Quantum: Both?" (#00FFFF) and show a coin spinning.
Show the coin blurred to represent multiple states.
Add labels "Heads" and "Tails" on opposite sides of the spinning coin.
The spinning coin glows, emphasizing it hasn't "chosen" yet.

            # Oscillation of width to simulate spin
            scale_x = np.cos(val * 2 * PI)
            # Avoid too-thin objects or zero scale
            w_factor = max(0.05, abs(scale_x))
            m[0].stretch_to_fit_width(w_factor * 1.4)
            
            # Switch between showing H and T
            if scale_x > 0:
                m[1].set_opacity(1)
                m[2].set_opacity(0)
                m[1].stretch_to_fit_width(max(0.05, abs(scale_x) * 0.8))
            else:
                m[1].set_opacity(0)
                m[2].set_opacity(1)
                m[2].stretch_to_fit_width(max(0.05, abs(scale_x) * 0.8))

        coin_group.add_updater(update_coin)
        
        self.add(coin_group)
        self.play(
            spin_tracker.animate.set_value(4), 
            FadeIn(h_side_label), 
            FadeIn(t_side_label),
            run_time=3, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Glow effect
        glow = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.15, stroke_width=0)
        glow.move_to(coin.get_center())
        
        def update_glow(m):
            # Pulsing effect
            pulse = np.sin(spin_tracker.get_value() * 3)
            m.set_fill(opacity=0.1 + 0.1 * abs(pulse))
            # Fixed scale updating logic to avoid recursive scaling
            target_width = 1.6 + 0.2 * pulse
            m.width = target_width
            m.height = target_width

        glow.add_updater(update_glow)
        
        self.add(glow)
        # Continue spinning and pulsing
        self.play(spin_tracker.animate.set_value(10), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2)

        y_tip = self.grid["C2"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: Quantum Computing",
            [
                "Classical bits process one path at a time.",
                "Qubits explore every possible path simultaneously.",
                "This allows computers to solve complex problems instantly."
            ]
        )

        # Maze Setup
        # Using Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg
        maze = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg")
        maze.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(maze, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        start_label = Text("START", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(start_label, 'F5', scale_factor=0.8) # Resolved Issue 47
        
        exit_label = Text("EXIT", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(exit_label, 'B6', scale_factor=0.8) # Resolved Issue 48

        self.add(maze, start_label, exit_label)

        # Define points for the classical path and quantum spread
        # Maze occupies roughly B2 to E5 area
        p_start = self.grid["E5"]
        path_points = [
            self.grid["E4"],
            self.grid["D4"],
            self.grid["D3"],
            self.grid["C3"],
            self.grid["C4"],
            self.grid["B4"],
            self.grid["B5"]
        ]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # White dot representing a classical bit
        white_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        white_dot.move_to(p_start)
        self.add(white_dot)
        
        # Sequential path movement
        for pos in path_points:
            self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(pos), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset color and highlight second line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF") # Cyan-like for Qubits
        
        # Reset white dot for comparison
        self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(p_start), run_time=0.5)

        # Create many blue dots to represent a superposition "gas"
        # We scatter them across the grid points inside the maze area
        blue_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.07) for _ in range(16)])
        for dot in blue_dots:
            dot.move_to(p_start)
        self.add(blue_dots)

        # Destinations for dots to simulate "filling" the maze
        scatter_points = [
            self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B3"], self.grid["B4"], self.grid["B5"],
            self.grid["C2"], self.grid["C3"], self.grid["C4"], self.grid["C5"],
            self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D4"], self.grid["D5"],
            self.grid["E2"], self.grid["E3"], self.grid["E4"], self.grid["E5"]
        ]

        # Animate blue dots spreading simultaneously
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[dot.animate.move_to(dest) for dot, dest in zip(blue_dots, scatter_points)],
                lag_ratio=0.03
            ),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset color and highlight third line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # The dot at the exit (B5) pulses
        exit_qubit = blue_dots[3] # Index 3 is B5 in the scatter_points list
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(exit_qubit, color=GREEN, scale_factor=2.0),
            white_dot.animate.move_to(path_points[0]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Show classical dot still trying while quantum is done
        self.play(white_dot.animate.move_to(path_points[1]), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measuring a system forces it to pick one state.",
            "The vector instantly snaps to a single classical axis.",
            "This sudden change is known as 'Wavefunction Collapse'.",
            "Probability depends on the square of the state's amplitude.",
            "The mystery of 'both' vanishes upon our observation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Collapse: The Act of Measuring", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PSI = "#FF69B4"   # Pink from section 3
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for |0> (Y-axis)
        COLOR_ALPHA = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_BETA = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_CAMERA = "#CCCCCC" # Grey
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Coordinate system - Adjusted per Issue 44
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'F5')
        
        label_0 = MathTex("|0\\rangle", color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(0.8)
        label_0.next_to(axes.c2p(0, 1), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        label_1 = MathTex("|1\\rangle", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        label_1.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Initial Vector |psi> at 45 degrees
        vec_end_init = axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5))
        vec_psi = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            end=vec_end_init,
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_PSI
        )
        label_psi = MathTex("|\\psi\\rangle", color=COLOR_PSI).scale(0.8)
        label_psi.next_to(vec_psi.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # Projections
        proj_alpha = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_ALPHA
        )
        proj_beta = DashedLine(
            axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), np.sqrt(0.5)), 
            color=COLOR_BETA
        )
        
        label_alpha = MathTex("\\alpha", color=COLOR_ALPHA).scale(0.8)
        label_alpha.next_to(axes.c2p(np.sqrt(0.5), 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        label_beta = MathTex("\\beta", color=COLOR_BETA).scale(0.8)
        label_beta.next_to(axes.c2p(0, np.sqrt(0.5)), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Camera Icon - Updated per Issue 32 & 45
        camera = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg")
        camera.set_color(COLOR_CAMERA)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.add(axes, label_0, label_1)
        self.play(Create(vec_psi), Write(label_psi))
        self.play(Create(proj_alpha), Create(proj_beta), Write(label_alpha), Write(label_beta))
        self.play(FadeIn(camera))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Preparation for snap: ghosts
        ghost_psi = vec_psi.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        ghost_proj_alpha = proj_alpha.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        ghost_label_alpha = label_alpha.copy().set_opacity(0.3)

        # Flash effect - Asset usage updated per Issue 32 (camera flashes)
        flash = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(camera.get_center())
        self.play(flash.animate.scale(50).set_opacity(0), run_time=0.4)
        self.remove(flash)
        
        # Add ghosts to scene
        self.add(ghost_psi, ghost_proj_alpha, ghost_label_alpha)

        # Vector snaps to Y-axis |0>
        target_end = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        self.play(
            vec_psi.animate.put_start_and_end_on(axes.c2p(0,0), target_end).set_color(COLOR_ZERO),
            label_psi.animate.next_to(target_end, UP, buff=0.1).set_color(COLOR_ZERO),
            proj_beta.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0),
            proj_alpha.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0),
            label_beta.animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO),
            run_time=0.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Emphasize collapse
        self.play(Indicate(vec_psi, color=COLOR_ZERO, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Show probability relationship - Updated per Issue 46
        prob_math = MathTex("P(|0\\rangle) = |\\beta|^2", color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_math, 'D6', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(prob_math))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Fade out ghosts and extra indicators
        self.play(
            FadeOut(ghost_psi),
            FadeOut(ghost_proj_alpha),
            FadeOut(ghost_label_alpha),
            FadeOut(camera),
            FadeOut(label_alpha),
            FadeOut(label_beta),
            prob_math.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
